name: Pebl Alfie
operator: Pebl (the vendor); each customer is the operator of its own use
basis: Pebl's own public pages (the Alfie product page and its FAQ, news releases, platform updates, llms.txt and API description)
what: An AI assistant embedded in Pebl's employer-of-record platform that answers global employment questions, builds workforce reports from the customer's Pebl data, and submits or approves time-off requests for the user who asks.
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the field agent from a company met at Web Summit 2026 (stand E163; data/intake/pebl.json): a researcher-assessor, a challenger, then the scorer. Pebl has not seen it.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

findings.finding: I15 says the person operates and every action is prompted and controlled by them. The cited FAQ sentence is 'We do not share your data with third parties except when required to generate a response or take an action that you request.' That sentence is about data sharing; it shows that an action can follow a user request, and says nothing about control or about who decides. The same product page lists 'Proactive guidance and recommended next steps' and the June 2026 release lists 'Dynamic follow-up prompts that guide employees toward actions', so the page also shows Alfie prompting the user. The scan's own note admits no source says whether Alfie asks for confirmation. I read this as an inference, not a documented fact, and the Autonomy level of 1 rests on it alone (I07 needs I02 to I05 for level 2, I16 is not credited). Without I15 Autonomy is 0 and the card would not meet the no-card-below-level-one rule, so this credit decides whether a card exists. The better-supported fact on the page is I08, which sits uneasily beside the level name Assists ('a person does each step'). Suggest: lower I15 or keep it with a stated caveat on the card, and resolve the open item (read the help-centre articles in a browser for any confirm step). Mode default is acceptable: the page says 'Alfie usage is optional' for each user and gives no switch for the action features.

Arguing against I08 as asked. Against: every source is the vendor's own marketing (a press release standfirst, a product page, an FAQ); no help-centre or documentation page was read, so how Alfie acts, whether it asks for confirmation and whether an admin must enable the action features are all unknown. The release quote from the CEO says Alfie is 'helping teams actually execute work inside a conversation', which can be read as user-driven. For: the release says 'Alfie completes approvals, workforce requests, reporting, and global employment workflows directly inside Pebl' (13 words, found exactly), and also 'AI that actively completes work'; the product page says 'Complete everyday workforce tasks directly through Alfie. Submit or approve time off' and lists 'Submit and approve time-off requests'; the FAQ list includes 'Submit or approve time-off requests'; and the release says the expanded capabilities 'are available now to Pebl customers'. I08 is 'It executes actions itself', set against I07 where a person acts; a statement that Alfie submits and approves time off meets that at documented grade, mode default (no page names an opt-in). The credit stands. It does not change the card: Autonomy 3 needs I08 plus one of I17, I18, I19, and I17 is not credited. I agree with the challenger dropping I17: no source says Alfie handles routine tasks and consults a person only on exceptions.

Note and source do not match. The note's second clause, 'the product page lists submitting and approving time-off requests', is not on the cited source (the June 2026 release); it is on the product page, which is the source of other answers. The release names 'time-off requests and approvals' but not submitting. Either cite the product page as the source of I08 (it is the stronger one: 'Submit and approve time-off requests') or remove the clause. No effect on the level.

The note says Alfie gives guidance, reports and recommended next steps 'that the user then acts on'. The span 'Proactive guidance and recommended next steps' is on the product page, but no source says the user then acts; the same page says Alfie submits and approves time off (I08). I07 is 'It retrieves information and recommends actions; a person acts', so crediting it beside I08 is a tension the note does not mention. Credit is defensible for the recommending half (the page lists recommended next steps and reporting), but the note should drop 'that the user then acts on' or say the page also lists actions Alfie takes. No effect on the level (I07 is used only with I02 to I05).

The note says 'the terms of use repeat this for all Pebl AI tools'. The terms of use are not a source of the scan, and the FAQ only links the Terms of Use in a different passage (ownership of outputs about employment law). Nothing on the cited page says the terms repeat the oversight statement. Remove the clause. The rest is exact on the product page (in the embedded FAQ data): 'AI can make mistakes. Users must ensure appropriate human oversight when using AI generated content.' and 'Outputs from Pebl AI are not legal, tax, or other professional advice.' Span of 10 words is in the source. Grade documented, mode default correct.

The note's last clause, 'the December 2025 release says Alfie Support draws on Pebl's indexed help centre and global employment database', cites a page that is not a source of the scan (the December 2025 release appears only under not_credited, and I could not find the words 'indexed' or 'Alfie Support' in any of the five sources). Remove it or add the page as a source. The FAQ part is on the page: 'Our proprietary models are trained on vetted global hiring documentation' and 'Alfie may leverage your Pebl account data to provide contextual answers'. Span of 11 words is in the source. Credit is right for I58.

The note cites a December 2025 release ('Alfie Support routes such questions to a specialist') that is not a source of the scan and whose words are not in the cited launch release. Remove it. The launch release (8 October 2025) does say 'Instant Support: Conversational, context-aware answers with seamless handoff to a human expert when needed.' The span is exact, grade documented, mode default. I40 asks for a defined escalation path; the page states a handoff, with no description of who or how, so the credit is thin. It feeds no level.

The span 'embedded across Pebl's global employment platform' is on the product page and shows Alfie inside one product. The note adds 'payroll and invoice data': invoices are on the product page ('Invoice charge breakdowns'), payroll is not on that page (it is on the platform updates page and in the June release). Minor; either cite or trim. Credit to I09 and R1 is right; I01 also gives R1 alone.
Span 'Alfie was built and is maintained by Pebl' is in the FAQ ('Yes, Alfie was built and is maintained by Pebl'); the apostrophe style differs only. Credit right, mode default.

Span 'purpose-built to be used as an HR tool' is in the FAQ answer to 'Did Pebl build Alfie?'. The note's list of uses is in the FAQ answer to 'What can Alfie help me do?' on the same page. Credit right; O1 rests on I20 with I22 and I58, all three verified.

Span 'Alfie inherits platform permissions, it does not bypass them' is in the FAQ answer on data access, with 'Every interaction with Alfie respects existing role-level based permissions.' The note's 'personal data is processed only as needed' is not quoted in the span and I did not check it; it is harmless. Control 1 rests on this one prose statement, which is an artefact of text, not an adjective, and the scan states that it does not say what enforces the limit.

FAQ answer to 'Which LLMs power Alfie?' reads 'This includes Claude by Anthropic, ChatGPT by OpenAI, Gemini by Google and Cortex by Snowflake'. Span exact (13 words), no versions, as noted. Grade documented, mode default.

Figures in the note are all in the June 2026 release (83.5%, 98.2%, more than 60%, 42%, 18%); the release does not say how they were measured, as the note says. Tier declared, grade documented is right for a vendor statement. Feeds no level. Not S1: the figures are deflection rates and ticket reductions, not sessions, tasks or pull requests, so leaving S1 uncredited is correct, and the Myers-Holum quote is about data Alfie provided.

The platform updates page renders only three entries (5 November, 27 October, 17 September 2026), so the page is paginated and JS-driven. The embedded page data holds the other dated Alfie entries named in the note: 4 June, 30 June (prompt suggestion cards), 27 August (currency conversion and saved reports), 27 October, 5 November. Dates match. Span 'Your payroll calendar, now connected to Alfie' is on the page. The 'structured program' clause is on the FAQ page, not this one; say so in the note. Feeds no level.

https://hellopebl.com/llms.txt returned 200 for me and lists 'Platform | Pebl Platform | Alfie AI Assistant'. Grade observed, mode default right. It is a site-wide index, not an Alfie-specific file, which the note says. The note also says the OpenAPI at developer.hellopebl.com resolves and has no Alfie endpoint: I fetched it (200, no occurrence of Alfie, time-off endpoints exist), but that page is not a source of the scan. S4 uncredited is right: it is the platform API, not documented for agents. S3 only matters for Openness 3, which also needs I50 (not credited).

Card A1 R1 C1 O2. No level 3 or 4 on the card, so no level 3 or 4 argument is needed. A1 rests on I15 (see finding), R1 on I09 or I01, C1 on I47, O2 on I22, I58, I61 (count 2 of 3 needed; all three verified). The next unlock for Autonomy is I17, which the sources do not support. Sources: the product page FAQ is only in the page's embedded JSON in my fetch (the visible text shows the questions as collapsed headings); the spans exist there. All five sources resolved. Not read by the scan or by me: the help-centre articles, which may settle I15 or I16.

responses.response: Lowered to not credited, as the finding allows: the sentence is about data sharing and the help-centre articles (read in a browser) do not settle I15 or I16. The card's Autonomy is therefore not yet evidenced, although I08 says Alfie acts; the Autonomy ladder has no rung for an agent that acts with no stated mode (A3 needs I17 to I19 beside I08). That is a rule question, asked of gamma-ray@ in team/requests.md; until it is answered the card stays below level one in Autonomy and must not be published.

Source moved to the product page, as suggested: 'Submit and approve time-off requests' (5 words, verified in the capture). The note now says only what that page says, with the June release named as saying the same. Credit, grade and mode unchanged.
Note corrected: 'that the user then acts on' removed; it now says the same page also lists actions Alfie takes (I08).
Clause about the terms of use removed.
Clause citing the December 2025 release removed.

Answered before this round arrived, then trimmed: the source is now the help article 'What is Alfie?' (read in a browser; text also in the captured page's embedded data), which says Alfie offers to open a support inquiry and passes the conversation to the Operations team. The December 2025 and launch-release clauses are gone. Still thin, as the reviewer says; it feeds no level.
'payroll' removed from the note; the rest is on the product page.
Note now says the structured program clause is on the product page's FAQ, not on the updates page, and that most entries sit in the embedded data.

open: Whether Alfie asks the user to confirm before it submits or approves time off (I15 or I16): the three help-centre articles on Alfie (read in a browser on 2026-11-10) do not say.
I63: Pebl states ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2 for the company; no report or scope covering Alfie was read; left not credited, as the Replit challenger did.
assessment.files: in the vault: work/assessment.json, work/challenger.json, work/rendered/ (help-centre articles as rendered in a browser)

added_after_challenge.why: The help centre's Alfie articles were read in a headless browser after the challenge; not yet challenged, left for review.
Re-sourced to the help article, which says it more directly; same credit.

I01.n: Pebl's FAQ says Pebl built and maintains Alfie, which customers use inside the Pebl platform as supplied.
I01.span: Alfie was built and is maintained by Pebl

I07.n: The product page lists proactive guidance, reports and recommended next steps among what Alfie gives; the same page also lists actions Alfie takes itself (I08).
I07.span: Proactive guidance and recommended next steps

I08.n: The product page lists submitting and approving time-off requests among what Alfie does, and says everyday workforce tasks are completed directly through Alfie. The June 2026 release says the same of approvals and workforce requests. No page names an opt-in for these actions.

I09.n: Alfie works inside Pebl's global employment platform, on that platform's employment, compensation, time-off and invoice data.
I09.span: embedded across Pebl’s global employment platform

I20.n: The FAQ states Alfie's purpose as an HR tool and lists what customers can use it for, including guidance, reports and submitting or approving time off.
I20.span: purpose-built to be used as an HR tool

I22.n: The FAQ says AI can make mistakes, that users must keep human oversight, and that outputs are not legal, tax or professional advice.
I22.span: AI can make mistakes. Users must ensure appropriate human oversight

I23.n: Pebl's help article enumerates, in a table per platform role (Company Admin, HR Manager, PTO Manager, Billing Admin, Supported Employee), which Alfie features each role can use, among them support tickets, time-off requests and approvals, compensation reports and currency conversion. It is a statement of scope; no source shows how it is enforced. The article's text is in the captured page's embedded data and shows only in a browser; the rendered text is in the vault (work/rendered/).
I23.span: What Can I Do With Alfie Based on My Role?

I40.n: Pebl's help article says that when a request needs human review or cannot be answered with confidence, Alfie offers to open a support inquiry and passes the conversation to Pebl's Operations team. It does not say who handles it beyond that team, or how. The article's text is in the captured page's embedded data and shows only in a browser; the rendered text is in the vault (work/rendered/).
I40.span: Alfie will automatically offer to open a support inquiry

I47.n: The FAQ states in prose that every interaction with Alfie respects the user's role-level permissions and that Alfie does not bypass them; it also says personal data is processed only as needed for a response.
I47.span: Alfie inherits platform permissions, it does not bypass them

I58.n: The FAQ says Pebl's own models are trained on vetted global hiring documentation and that Alfie may use the customer's Pebl account data.
I58.span: Alfie may leverage your Pebl account data to provide contextual answers

I61.n: The FAQ names the model families Alfie uses: Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT (OpenAI), Gemini (Google) and Cortex (Snowflake), plus Pebl's own models; no versions are given.
I61.span: Claude by Anthropic, ChatGPT by OpenAI, Gemini by Google and Cortex by Snowflake

I67.n: The June 2026 release states figures for Alfie: an 83.5% support ticket deflection rate and 98.2% for global hiring and compliance questions; it says customers cut reporting requests by more than 60%, compensation inquiries by 42% and time-off tickets by 18%. It does not say how they were measured.
I67.span: achieving an 83.5% support ticket deflection rate

I68.n: The platform updates page lists dated Alfie changes in 2026: 4 June (benefits), 30 June (prompt cards), two on 27 August (currency conversion, saved reports), 27 October (invoices) and 5 November (payroll calendar); most entries sit in the page's embedded data, the rendered page shows three. The intervals are not fixed. A structured program to improve AI accuracy is stated on the Alfie product page's FAQ, not on this page, with no cycle given.
I68.span: Your payroll calendar, now connected to Alfie

S3.n: An llms.txt resolves at hellopebl.com (fetched 2026-11-10); it is the platform-wide site index, in which the Alfie page is one entry. An OpenAPI description of the Pebl Public API also resolves at developer.hellopebl.com, without any Alfie endpoint.
S3.span: Platform | Pebl Platform | Alfie AI Assistant

not_credited.what: S1: the June 2026 release gives usage figures (83.5% ticket deflection, 98.2% for hiring and compliance questions, reporting requests down more than 60%, time-off tickets down 18%) and quotes a benefits manager at Myers-Holum, Inc; Pebl's product page carries the same quote.
not_credited.why: The figures measure questions deflected and requests avoided, and the quote is about data Alfie provided; none counts tasks Alfie completed (time-off submissions or approvals). The 'thousands of workforce conversations' predate the action features. No source names a customer using Alfie to act.

not_credited.what: I12: the December 2025 release says Alfie became 'two coordinated AI agents', Alfie Reporting and Alfie Support.
not_credited.why: The release names two specialised functions but describes no coordination between them (no handoff or passing of work), and the current product page and June 2026 release present one Alfie. Too thin for several agents coordinating.

not_credited.what: I10: Alfie covers compensation, time off, payroll calendars, invoices, benefits and onboarding.
not_credited.why: All of these are data and workflows inside the one Pebl platform; no source says Alfie works across other systems.

not_credited.what: I11: the FAQ says data is shared with third parties when required to generate a response or take an action the user requests, and Alfie uses third-party models.
not_credited.why: Calling model providers is how it runs, not a connection to external tools; no integration of Alfie with an outside system is described. Pebl's HRIS integrations are the platform's, not Alfie's.

not_credited.what: I56: Pebl names the product 'Alfie AI Assistant' on its marketing pages, and the help portal greets visitors with an invitation to ask its AI assistant.
not_credited.why: Both are addressed to buyers or portal visitors; no source says the Alfie interface tells employees and managers they are talking to an AI.

not_credited.what: I57: handoff to a human expert and smart-routing to specialists.
not_credited.why: These route a question Alfie cannot answer to a person; no source describes a channel to report a problem with Alfie or contest its output. The site's SpeakUp! hotline is a company whistleblowing line, not for Alfie.

not_credited.what: I63: the security page states Pebl is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified and has a SOC 2 Type 2 report.
not_credited.why: Organisational statements; no certificate or report was read (the Vanta trust centre did not render without JavaScript) and no scope says it covers Alfie. Not counted as an independent check yet.

not_credited.what: I45: the FAQ says Alfie inherits platform permissions and does not bypass them.
not_credited.why: The Spectrum-card reading of I45 does count a documented limit enforced outside the agent, so 'operation indicator, no artefact' is not the reason. The reason is that the FAQ ('inherits platform permissions, it does not bypass them') does not say what enforces the limit (a data-access layer, scoped tokens, or an instruction to the model). Credited as a rule in prose (I47).

not_credited.what: I41: the FAQ says Alfie inputs and outputs are stored, encrypted, in an AWS database in the US.
not_credited.why: Storage of conversations, not a log of actions; operation indicator with no artefact.

not_credited.what: I43, I51: the security page names automated alerts, 24/7 on-call engineering, and continuously scanned repositories with automated security rules.
not_credited.why: Platform-wide claims, not about Alfie; operation indicators with no artefact.

not_credited.what: S4: the Pebl Public API (OpenAPI at developer.hellopebl.com) lets approved partners submit and review time-off requests, generate offers and read compensation.
not_credited.why: It exposes Pebl's platform, not Alfie, and is not described for agents to call; no MCP server or agent card was found.

not_credited.what: I61 (second source): the privacy policy says chats with Pebl's 'AI-powered chat assistant' may be shared with Abacus.AI.
not_credited.why: The section is in the part about visitors to the site and does not name Alfie; it is not used for I61, which rests on the Alfie FAQ.

not_credited.what: I65: the June 2026 release and the September 2025 rebrand present Pebl as 'AI-first' and Alfie as moving from assistant to workforce agent.
not_credited.why: Product positioning in press releases, not a stated strategy for agents.

not_credited.what: I17: Alfie Support answers routine questions and routes those needing human expertise to a Pebl specialist.
not_credited.why: A handoff of a support conversation (credited as I40), not the agent carrying out routine tasks on its own with a person consulted on exceptions; every named action is made at the user's request (I15).

not_credited.what: I25: the FAQ says Alfie respects each user's role-level permissions; an employee can ask only about their own data; only account admins can generate reports with Alfie.
not_credited.why: Alfie inherits the user's own access, which is the same as the user's account, not narrower. The report restriction is not shown to be narrower than what those roles can do elsewhere in the platform.

not_credited.what: I15: the FAQ says Pebl shares data only to answer or to "take an action that you request".
not_credited.why: Lowered after review round one: the sentence is about data sharing and shows only that an action can follow a request; no source says who controls each action, and the pages also show Alfie prompting the user (recommended next steps, follow-up prompts). Pebl's three help-centre articles on Alfie, read in a browser on 2026-11-10, do not say whether Alfie asks for confirmation before it acts, so I16 is not evidenced either. Not evidenced is not no.

announced.what: Proactive compliance: Alfie will alert teams to regulatory changes before they take effect (marked coming soon, October 2025).
Country-specific benefits answers in Alfie are marked coming soon in the US.

configurations.name: As shipped
configurations.note: Alfie as embedded in the Pebl platform for Pebl customers, with what it may read and do set by the user's role (employee, manager, company admin).
